items.title: Sahasrara
level: The top level is in charge of the link to a bigger plan: why any of this, and what stays behind afterwards. While it keeps quiet a person lives perfectly well, but every so often runs into the question “and what then” — and no pay rise ever answers it.

A strong Sahasrara gives the calm of someone who knows their place in something larger: they do not shrink into squabbles and tell the important from the merely urgent. An empty one pulls either into cynicism (“there is nothing”) or into somebody else’s teaching, where ready-made meaning is handed out at the door.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: In matter this is about the end result: which of a person’s deeds outlive them — what they wrote, what they built, the people they taught. The same column shows whether they manage to do anything not only for themselves.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Gives a reserve of meaning that strength is drawn from in the hard years. With that reserve a person comes through losses without falling apart; with none, they break on the first serious injustice.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: Felt as quiet gratitude and a sense that life is not an accident. Out of balance it turns into either exaltation and an endless search for a teacher, or a cold emptiness in which everything looks pointless.

items.title: Ajna
level: Ajna is about seeing. Not eyesight, but the knack of working out in advance where a venture will end up, and of catching the main thing in a conversation. A strong level is recognised by what people around say: “how did you know”.

When this level is skewed, a person either distrusts their own guesses and regrets it every time afterwards, or believes any thought that arrives at night. The fix is plain and dull: check hunches against facts and keep score — after a year it is clear where the instinct is and where the worry is.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: Shows what seeing turns into in practice: planning, strategy, work with other people’s ideas. A weak column looks like good ideas that never make it as far as a timetable.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Feeds intuition and curiosity. This column shows the way a person learns: one needs a teacher and a structure, another just sits in silence and works it all out alone.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: About trusting yourself. At its best, a calm confidence in your own reading of a situation; at its worst, nagging pictures of the future that frighten more than anything real ever does.

items.title: Vishuddha
level: Vishuddha is in charge of the word, and of the fate that builds up out of what gets said. Everything to do with honesty lands here: whether a person keeps promises, calls things by their names, can say “no” without three days of preparation.

This level shows up most clearly in career and reputation. A strong Vishuddha gives a voice people believe and the timing to say the right thing; a blocked one gives a lump in the throat, an endless “I will keep quiet, it will sort itself out”, and grudges nobody but their owner knows about.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: The work where a voice turns into a result: negotiations, texts, teaching, sales. The column also shows whether a person is paid for what they say and write.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Puts drive into a conversation and carries the weight of someone else’s pressure without snapping and without going silent. An empty column: the voice gives out exactly when it is time to answer.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: Honesty with yourself lives here. At its best a person says what they think and is calm once the talk is over; at its worst they store up the unsaid, then pour it all out at once and at the wrong person.

items.title: Anahata
level: Anahata is the level of love and relationships, and it is measured not by the number of romances but by the ability to stay close without losing yourself. A strong column here shows in one simple sign: other people are not afraid around such a person.

The skew goes two ways. A closed Anahata keeps its distance and explains it away as being busy; one thrown wide open gives everything and demands the same back, sending a bill for every act of care. The working state sits between these extremes: open, but with boundaries.

Closer to the centre than any other level: the left number of this row stands between the inner left point and the centre, the right one between the inner point of talent and the centre. That is why the level reads as the most personal — it is nearer to who someone is alone with themselves than to how others see them.

The third number of the row is not taken from the chart on its own — it is the sum of the first two, reduced. It shows no new theme, only what those two add up to when a person is in their feelings. Reading the row by one number is therefore pointless: a triple like “9 7 16” tells a single story, in which the third follows from the first two instead of arguing with them.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: Shows what love turns into day to day: who cooks the soup, who pays, who keeps the house running. An empty column looks like big feelings with no shared life behind them.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Answers for the ability to carry a relationship for years — through quarrels, dull spells and boredom. The parental reserve sits here too: how much warmth a person can give away without running empty.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: The core: how attachment is felt and what someone does with jealousy, hurt and tenderness. In the minus it is either icy politeness or life on an emotional swing.

items.title: Manipura
level: Will, standing and money — that is Manipura. This is the level where it is settled whether a person carries their own thing through to a result and whether they can name a price. A strong Manipura is not necessarily loud: you see it in the fact that decisions get done.

A weak level looks familiar: plenty of work, little money, I agree to somebody else’s terms and then get angry about it. An overheated one is trouble as well: power for the sake of power, a race for status, and irritation at everyone who will not obey. The tuning goes through boundaries — first learn to refuse, then learn to ask for more.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: Straight about money and position: how much a person earns, what they own, how they behave in a bargain. It also shows the line below which they should not be agreeing to anything.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Gives will and the power to push a thing through. A full column means someone does not fall apart at a refusal and goes to the end; an empty one means a good start and then waiting for somebody else to decide.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: This column is about anger and dignity. Anger in good order lifts a person and guards their boundaries; suppressed, it turns into resentment towards those who do well; overheated, into contempt for the weak.

items.title: Svadhisthana
level: Svadhisthana answers for joy, children and creative work — for everything done not by calculation but because you want to. The level is often underrated, yet it is what holds motivation up: without it any correct life turns into hard labour within a year.

The check is simple: when did the person last do something with no aim and no use in it? A strong column gives a taste for life and ease in the body; a blocked one gives “I have no time”, shame about pleasure, and rest that looks like lying down with a phone and gives nothing back.

Where this level stands in the chart: the left number is the entry of the money line, point L, and the right one the entry of relationships and the karmic tail, point M. Both lie on the inner rhombus, level with the centre. Hence the sense of the row: joy is not a separate topic here, it is what pays for both work and closeness.

The right number has a quirk you can spot at once on your own chart: point M only ever carries numbers divisible by three — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. Nothing else lands there, whatever the date of birth. The left number is free and takes any value from 3 to 22, so the pair almost never matches, and it has to be read as two different questions rather than one.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: What a person makes with their hands for pleasure and how they treat their body: food, movement, sex, craft. Children belong here in the most everyday sense too — playing, messing about, spending time for no reason at all.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: The source of live interest. A full column means ideas and wants arrive by themselves; an empty one means someone runs on willpower and coffee, with nothing left to want.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: About being able to enjoy things and to allow yourself something good. In the minus: guilt over pleasure, envy of people who know how to rest, and slips into snacking or other quick comforts.

items.title: Muladhara
level: Muladhara is the support: the body, a home, money for the month ahead, the feeling of standing on solid ground. It is the lowest level of all, and it holds up every other one — without it the higher meanings hang in the air and any plan gets derailed by everyday chores.

A strong Muladhara looks unremarkable from the outside: the person sleeps, eats, pays the bills and does not panic at the word “crisis”. A weak one brings constant worry about tomorrow even when money is fine, the habit of living out of a suitcase, and a body that gets attention last of all.

columns.title: Physics
columns.text: The most literal column of the three: body, stamina, a place to live, money left in the account. It shows whether a person has a foundation solid enough to build something lasting on.

columns.title: Energy
columns.text: Gives staying power and the ability to hold on when everything is falling apart. A full column means a person gets back on their feet with sleep and a proper meal; an empty one means a single conversation drains them and every change of season knocks them out of action.

columns.title: Emotions
columns.text: This is about the basic sense of safety. At its best it gives calm and trust in life; at its worst, a fear of not having enough, which makes a person accept bad terms and then cling to them.
